title: First Rule of Entrepreneurship: There Are No Rules
coreMove: Keep judgment alive by testing whether a rule fits the present facts before applying it.
sourcePressure: The chapter rejects universal formulas while preserving principles; timing, leverage, trust, creativity, accountability, and changing facts determine whether a rule still fits.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version is rules do not matter, so entrepreneurs should improvise boldly.

hook: rules are made to be broken

exampleSpecs.domain: pharmaceutical cold-chain courier negotiating a hospital exception
exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatch director deciding whether to violate the standard route rule
exampleSpecs.stakes: the usual route protects efficiency, but a transplant shipment needs a different risk calculation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director writes the principle behind the route rule, compares it with the transplant deadline, and approves a one-time escort with extra temperature checks
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a sealed transplant medication case beside a printed route matrix

exampleSpecs.domain: independent game studio deciding whether to delay a creative milestone
exampleSpecs.audience: a studio head balancing creative space against publisher accountability
exampleSpecs.stakes: strict milestone enforcement may kill the mechanic that could save the game
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the studio head separates the accountability principle from the calendar rule and trades a two-week delay for a playable mechanic proof
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a build screen paused on an unfinished combat mechanic

exampleSpecs.domain: community bank deciding whether to keep a loan policy during flood recovery
exampleSpecs.audience: a lending officer whose standard collateral rule blocks otherwise viable local businesses
exampleSpecs.stakes: rigid policy could harm the town, but loose lending could damage the bank
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the officer names the risk principle, designs a temporary flood-recovery covenant, and schedules review dates instead of simply waiving policy
exampleSpecs.firstImage: mud-stained loan files drying on a plastic folding table

exampleSpecs.domain: airline maintenance hangar after a rare parts shortage
exampleSpecs.audience: a maintenance chief deciding whether the no-cannibalization rule still fits
exampleSpecs.stakes: grounded aircraft and safety standards collide under a shortage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the chief records why the rule exists, authorizes one documented parts transfer, and adds a return-to-standard trigger
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a grounded aircraft with a missing access panel tagged in orange

exampleSpecs.domain: publishing house handling a surprise rights auction
exampleSpecs.audience: an editor deciding whether to break the imprint's normal bid ceiling
exampleSpecs.stakes: the rule protects margin, but the author could reshape the list if timing and trust are read correctly
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the editor predicts what the ceiling rule protects, tests the current leverage with the agent, and raises the bid only after naming the new constraint
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rights auction email open beside a marked-up acquisition P&L

exampleSpecs.domain: industrial design firm choosing whether to bypass its client signoff sequence
exampleSpecs.audience: a project lead whose medical device prototype must hit a regulatory demo
exampleSpecs.stakes: standard signoff prevents rework, but the demo window will close before the usual sequence ends
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the lead states the principle behind signoff, creates a narrower prototype-only approval path, and logs what cannot ship under that exception
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a foam medical-device prototype sitting beside an unsigned approval packet

skillTargets: judge whether current context changes application
avoid using policy as shelter from tradeoff
evaluate exceptions with boundaries and return triggers

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one rule you are about to enforce. Write the principle it protects, the current fact that may change its fit, and the boundary that would make an exception legitimate.
sourceAnchorsNote: source contains no named anecdote for this chapter
